doc.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023

title: Seeing Nat King Cole at the Flamingo
summary: At about 12 he saw Nat Cole's dinner show, remembering 'Miss Otis Regrets' and Cole's joke about not playing his hit 'Rambling Rose'.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: went to but dinner shows, they had something they called the dinner show at that time and if there was anything risque about you know this show, a dinner show would be much milder in comparison. Kids were allowed to go because they served dinner — a technicality — and that’s how I got to see Nat Cole with my parents. They took me to see him at the Flamingo. I’ll never forget it.
Why? It’s an obvious question because of his musicianship, but I’m wondering if there was something beyond that that also caught your attention?

Musicianship front and center, and he was on piano which he played quite extensively during the show. This is a main room show in Las Vegas. Spectacular lighting. It somehow impressed me as a kid but because his Vegas show was such that each song was like a vignette. And I remember he did “Miss Otis Regrets” — I’d never heard the song before but it stuck with me, I know it now, and he was under kind of a street lamp with a Sinatraesque raincoat over his shoulder singing “Miss Otis Regrets” “she is unable to lunch today” — so elegant and that made an impression on me. And then what he said, you know some of the dialogue I even remember word for word because he had a hit at the time on the rock & roll radio, “Rambling Rose.”

“Why you ramble heaven knows.” I knew the song very well and his show, however, was more jazz than contemporary music. This would have been about ’62 when we were there you know. And so who knows how he felt about “Rambling Rose” I don’t know he sure sang the hell out of it, but when it was time for that he spoke to the audience and he said, “You know ladies and gentlemen at this time in the show a performer like myself would normally play what is currently and commonly referred to as his hit record but in some circles that would be referred to as milking the audience and you people have already been milked enough at the tables.” And even as a 12-year-old I said I better get this down word for word.
